benchmarks.title: Adults who gave regular care to a family member or friend (BRFSS 2025)
benchmarks.why: The simulator describes caregivers of people with dementia; this shows how common regular caregiving of any kind is among adults in the areas that asked
benchmarks.summary: In the 27 areas that asked the caregiver module, 23.4% of adults (weighted) said that in the past 30 days they provided regular care or assistance to a friend or family member with a health problem or disability: 37,131 of 154,632 answers (24.0% unweighted).

provenance.source_type: Federal telephone survey, self-report (CDC BRFSS, variable CAREGIV1)
provenance.origin: CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2025 public-use data file and codebook, downloaded from the CDC website by DBbun (SHA-256 of the data zip: be4a9f167480b1ad788640e21d8b265660c12c87d54c121839c746f29d8fb734)
provenance.reliability: Self-reported survey; weighted percentage as published by CDC in the codebook; counts reproduced from the data file and matching the codebook.

limits: Not specific to dementia: the person cared for has any health problem or disability.
Not a national estimate: only 27 areas asked this module (AK, AL, AZ, DE, FL, HI, IA, ID, IN, KS, LA, MN, MO, MT, ND, NH, NM, OR, PA, PR, RI, SC, TN, TX, VT, WA, WV).
Different population from the paper: it counts all adults in those areas, not the paper’s sample.

benchmarks.title: Caregivers whose care recipient also has Alzheimer’s, dementia or another cognitive impairment (BRFSS 2025)
benchmarks.why: The simulator describes caregivers of people with dementia; this shows what share of caregivers in the areas that asked say the person they care for has such a condition
benchmarks.summary: Among caregivers who answered the follow-up question in the 27 areas that asked, 14.5% (weighted) said the person they care for also has Alzheimer’s disease, dementia or another cognitive impairment disorder: 4,630 of 32,510 answers (14.2% unweighted).

provenance.source_type: Federal telephone survey, self-report (CDC BRFSS, variable CRGVALZD)
provenance.origin: CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2025 public-use data file and codebook, downloaded from the CDC website by DBbun (SHA-256 of the data zip: be4a9f167480b1ad788640e21d8b265660c12c87d54c121839c746f29d8fb734)
provenance.reliability: Self-reported survey; weighted percentage as published by CDC in the codebook; counts reproduced from the data file and matching the codebook.

limits: Asked only of caregivers, in 27 areas; not a national estimate.
The wording covers Alzheimer’s disease, dementia or another cognitive impairment, not dementia alone.

benchmarks.title: Adults 45 and over reporting memory or thinking difficulties that are happening more often or getting worse (BRFSS 2025)
benchmarks.why: Gives scale for self-reported cognitive change among middle-aged and older adults in the areas that asked
benchmarks.summary: In the 16 areas that asked the cognitive decline module, 19.2% of adults 45 and over (weighted) said that in the past 12 months they had difficulties with thinking or memory that were happening more often or getting worse: 15,184 of 74,780 answers (20.3% unweighted).

provenance.source_type: Federal telephone survey, self-report (CDC BRFSS, variable CIMEMLO1)
provenance.origin: CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2025 public-use data file and codebook, downloaded from the CDC website by DBbun (SHA-256 of the data zip: be4a9f167480b1ad788640e21d8b265660c12c87d54c121839c746f29d8fb734)
provenance.reliability: Self-reported survey; weighted percentage as published by CDC in the codebook; counts reproduced from the data file and matching the codebook.

limits: Self-report, not a diagnosis of dementia.
Not a national estimate: only 16 areas asked this module (CT, DE, GA, HI, IL, IN, KS, KY, MO, OR, PR, RI, TN, TX, WA, WI).

benchmarks.title: Deaths with Alzheimer’s disease or dementia as the underlying cause, United States, 2022 to 2024 (CDC NCHS)
benchmarks.why: Gives national scale for dementia as a cause of death, as context for the burdens the paper reports for people with dementia and their caregivers
benchmarks.summary: Death records with an underlying cause of Alzheimer’s disease (G30), vascular dementia (F01) or unspecified dementia (F03): 234,649 in 2022, 223,553 in 2023 and 224,680 in 2024.

provenance.source_type: Federal death records (NCHS public-use mortality files), counted by script
provenance.origin: CDC National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) public-use mortality files for 2022, 2023 and 2024 (death records)
provenance.reliability: Counts of records by underlying cause. The code positions in the file were checked only by whether the counts look plausible, not against the official record layout.

limits: Death records, not people living with dementia.
Only the underlying cause is counted, so deaths where dementia was a contributing cause are missed.
The record-layout check against the official NCHS layout has not been done; 2016 to 2021 were not read.
Not about caregivers, and not from the paper’s sample.
